Ghostline enforces honest, provider-aware data handling based on your active AI engine.
• Local Mode (Ollama): 100% on-device inference. Screenshots, OCR text, and microphone transcripts never leave your machine.

• Cloud Mode (BYOK): Prompts and question context are transmitted directly over encrypted HTTPS to your selected provider (e.g. Gemini, Groq, OpenAI). API keys are stored encrypted at rest using Windows DPAPI.
• Screen Capture Protection: Ghostline overlay window uses native Windows API (WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) to remain invisible to screen shares and meeting recordings.

Data handling policies, connection details, and privacy protections.
Ghostline is configured for 100% offline local inference via Ollama. No prompts, screen frames, transcripts, or queries leave your machine.
When using local Ollama inference, Ghostline binds strictly to local loopback (127.0.0.1). Zero network packets, screen content, transcripts, or questions ever leave your machine.
Local inference mode keeps all OCR, audio processing, questions, and responses on your computer.

When using cloud AI providers, your API keys are encrypted at rest using Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI CryptProtectData). Keys are cryptographically bound to your Windows user logon account and cannot be decrypted by other user accounts.
Keys are stored securely via Windows DPAPI and are never written in plaintext or uploaded to any third party.
Ghostline floating overlay windows leverage the Windows SetWindowDisplayAffinity (WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) API to prevent the HUD itself from appearing in screen shares, recordings, or self-captures.
Floating HUD overlays are automatically excluded from screen capture and screen share pipelines.

Which of the following data structures is most suitable for implementing an efficient priority queue with dynamic insertions?

A priority queue requires efficient retrieval of extreme elements. In a Binary Heap, elements can be inserted in O(log n) time and the minimum or maximum element can be extracted in O(log n) time, whereas an array or linked list would require O(n) for either insertion or extraction.
